us.summary: The register does not hold a systematic inventory of the United States space-industrial base; what it evidences is the trade and program interface with Australia. Northrop Grumman is the developer of the trilateral DARC deep-space radar, whose Exmouth site was completed in September 2024 under a US$341 million contract (EV-USSFCSPO-14). Lockheed Martin Australia was preferred tenderer for the JP9102 military SATCOM acquisition (April 2023) before Defence cancelled the procurement on 4 November 2024 (EV-DOMESTIC-10; EV-RONINS20-05, corrected wording). The AUKUS licence-free environment now covers most satellite hardware: the April 2024 EAR rule made over US$7.5 billion per year of trade licence-free (EV-AUKUSLFE-06); USSC estimates roughly 80 per cent of EAR-controlled and 70 per cent of ITAR-controlled US exports to Australia are now licence-free (EV-AUKUSLFE-12), with 210-plus Australian companies and A$25 million-plus in licence-free exports observed by February 2025 (EV-AUKUSLFE-13). The Technology Safeguards Agreement enables US companies to launch from Australia (EV-AUKUSLFE-17); launch-revenue projections are TO_VERIFY (EV-AUKUSLFE-20). Claimed Starlink resilience in Ukraine is uncorroborated blog material (EV-RONINS20-17, TO_VERIFY).

key_companies.name: Northrop Grumman
key_companies.note: DARC developer; Site 1 (Exmouth WA) completed September 2024 under a US$341 million contract (EV-USSFCSPO-14, EV-AUINPUTS-13).

key_companies.name: Lockheed Martin Australia
key_companies.note: JP9102 preferred tenderer April 2023; procurement cancelled 4 November 2024 before contract signature (EV-DOMESTIC-10; EV-RONINS20-05, corrected).

key_companies.name: Intelsat
key_companies.note: IS-22 18-channel UHF hosted payload (launched 2012); ~half capacity to US Navy in exchange for reciprocal MUOS access (EV-USSFCSPO-19).

key_companies.name: SpaceX (Starlink)
key_companies.note: Appears only via an uncorroborated register ASSESSMENT on Starlink resilience in Ukraine (EV-RONINS20-17, TO_VERIFY).

us.caveats: The register evidences the US industrial base only where it touches Australian programs and export rules. There is no inventory of US space primes, launch providers or commercial constellations; SpaceX/Starlink rests on one uncorroborated blog-derived record. US industrial capacity, workforce and space-control industry are register gaps (united-states.md paragraph 10).

uk.summary: The register cannot support a judgement of the United Kingdom's space-industrial base: the UK baseline's own gap note records no register material on UK military SATCOM (Skynet), PNT, ISR-EO, space science programs, sovereign SDA sensors other than DARC, industrial capacity or workforce scale (united-kingdom.md paragraph 3, TO_VERIFY). What is evidenced is narrow. Inmarsat, the UK-headquartered commercial SATCOM operator, is documented through the April 2023 I-4 F1 outage that disabled GPS-correction services for precision agriculture across four Australian states and New Zealand (EV-CONVERSA-15) — an Australian-dependency record rather than an industrial-base record. SaxaVord Spaceport (Shetland) is hosting Rocket Factory Augsburg's RFA ONE maiden-flight campaign under a UK CAA launch licence, after an August 2024 static-fire loss of the first stage (EV-GERMANY-16, ASSESSMENT, Medium). The UK's export-control machinery — the AUKUS open general licence in force 1 September 2024, carrying its own excluded-technology list — is treated by the register as an industrial-access capability in its own right (EV-AUKUSLFE-10, EV-AUKUSLFE-11). The DARC UK site at Cawdor Barracks, Wales, is US-prime work, expected complete by February 2030 (EV-USSFCSPO-14).

key_companies.name: Inmarsat
key_companies.note: UK-headquartered SATCOM operator; April 2023 I-4 F1 outage disabled GPS-correction for precision agriculture in four Australian states and NZ (EV-CONVERSA-15).

key_companies.name: SaxaVord Spaceport
key_companies.note: Shetland launch site hosting the RFA ONE maiden-flight campaign under a UK CAA licence (EV-GERMANY-16, ASSESSMENT).

uk.caveats: The UK industrial picture is a register gap, not a thin base: no records on Skynet, UK primes (e.g. no register record of Airbus UK or BAE space work), industrial capacity or workforce scale. Only two commercial entities appear at all, one of them via a Germany-topic record. TO_VERIFY across the board (united-kingdom.md paragraph 3 gap note).

japan.summary: The register's Japan industry coverage is explicitly thin: the baseline's evidence-quality section lists the commercial space-industrial base 'beyond single-company mentions' as missing (japan.md paragraph 10). What it holds: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' upgraded Mogami-class frigate was selected for the RAN general purpose frigate program (announced 5 August 2025; ~A$10 billion; first delivery 2029) — the first frigate Japan will manufacture for another nation, treated by the register as the pathfinder precedent for navigating Japan's export-policy constraints; it is not a space program (EV-JAPANAU-19, FACT). ASPI identifies Japanese maritime-domain-awareness ISR constellation projects, citing IHI Corporation, as a realistic Japan-Australia cooperation area (EV-JAPANAU-21, ASSESSMENT). A government-endorsed bilateral industry symposium covering space situational awareness, satellite communications and autonomous systems ran in Tokyo in November 2023 (EV-JAPANAU-16, FACT). Industrial flows remain gated by the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology and METI licensing under FEFTA, tightened in May 2025 and again from October 2025 (EV-JAPANAU-17, EV-JAPANAU-18, EV-EXPORTRE-15). Defence SATCOM, sovereign launch and the wider industrial base are collection gaps, not evidence of absence (japan.md paragraph 3).

key_companies.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
key_companies.note: Mogami-class frigate selected for the RAN general purpose frigate program, August 2025 — defence-industrial export precedent, not space (EV-JAPANAU-19).

key_companies.name: IHI Corporation
key_companies.note: Named by ASPI as an example of Japanese MDA-ISR constellation projects relevant to cooperation with Australia (EV-JAPANAU-21, ASSESSMENT).

japan.caveats: Only two companies are named anywhere in the Japan slice, one of them for a non-space program. Japan's space primes, defence SATCOM industry, launch sector (H3/H-IIA manufacturers as Japanese industry) and workforce are register silences logged in the japan.md validation backlog. The H-IIA appears only incidentally as the UAE Hope mission's launcher (EV-UAE-07).

india.summary: Indian industry is evidenced through the commercial launch interface with Australia and macro export figures rather than a company inventory. NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) is contracted to launch Space Machines Company's 450 kg Optimus spacecraft on a dedicated SSLV under Space MAITRI — the first dedicated Australia-India launch agreement, with A$8.5 million in Australian Government funding (EV-QUADINDI-12; EV-INDIACOC-08); launch timing has slipped and is unverified (india topic analyst note, TO_VERIFY). Space MAITRI embeds Indian industry deeply: Ananth Technologies provides assembly, integration and testing plus launch-site fuelling, and Indian SSA company Digantara supplies an electro-optical payload on Optimus to track resident space objects including debris (EV-INDIACOC-11, FACT). At the macro level, defence exports reached Rs 23,622 crore (~US$2.76 billion) in FY2024-25 to nearly 80 countries, a 34-fold rise on 2013-14 (EV-QUADINDI-13), with a declared target of Rs 50,000 crore annually by 2029 (EV-QUADINDI-14). Delivery capacity is the evidenced weakness: a CAG audit of post-Galwan Emergency Procurement found 72 per cent of examined contracts missed the one-year delivery timeline (EV-QUADINDI-18). SATCOM (GSAT), PNT (NavIC) and space-industrial workforce records are absent (india.md paragraph 3 gap note).

key_companies.name: NewSpace India Limited (NSIL)
key_companies.note: ISRO's commercial arm; dedicated SSLV launch for Space MAITRI/Optimus (EV-QUADINDI-12, EV-INDIACOC-08).

key_companies.name: Ananth Technologies
key_companies.note: Assembly, integration and testing (Bengaluru cleanrooms) plus launch-site fuelling for Space MAITRI (EV-INDIACOC-11).

key_companies.name: Digantara
key_companies.note: Indian SSA company supplying an electro-optical debris-tracking payload integrated on Optimus (EV-INDIACOC-11).

india.caveats: The register names Indian companies only where they touch Space MAITRI. India's satellite-manufacturing primes, launch-vehicle industry structure, GSAT/NavIC industry and workforce numbers are unpopulated register areas carried in the india.md validation backlog. Export figures are aggregate defence exports, not space-sector figures.

germany.summary: Germany's evidenced base is built around two primes and an applied-research institute. Airbus built SARah-1 (launched 18 June 2022) and is prime for SATCOMBw 3 — a ~€2.1 billion July 2024 contract for two geostationary military communications satellites plus ground segment, launch and 15 years of operation (EV-GERMANY-09, EV-GERMANY-10). OHB built SARah-2/3 (launched December 2023) and sits in the SATCOMBw 3 value chain (EV-GERMANY-09, EV-GERMANY-10); its Australian-linked SpaceLink investment wound down in 2022 and no operating OHB subsidiary in Australia was identified (EV-GERMANY-20, Medium confidence, negative finding). Fraunhofer FHR built the GESTRA LEO surveillance radar on a 2015 DLR commission (EV-GERMANY-08). No sovereign orbital launch capability is evidenced; German NewSpace launch firms are active abroad — Rocket Factory Augsburg's maiden campaign is centred on SaxaVord (UK) with a 2022 Whalers Way agreement assessed dormant (EV-GERMANY-15, EV-GERMANY-16), HyImpulse successfully launched and recovered its SR75 from Koonibba, South Australia, on 3 May 2024 (EV-GERMANY-17), and Isar Aerospace attempted the first orbital launch from continental Europe at Andøya on 30 March 2025 (EV-NORWAY-13). Workforce numbers are not held (germany.md paragraph 3).

key_companies.name: Airbus
key_companies.note: SARah-1 builder; SATCOMBw 3 prime (~€2.1 billion, July 2024) (EV-GERMANY-09, EV-GERMANY-10).

key_companies.name: OHB
key_companies.note: SARah-2/3 builder; SATCOMBw 3 value chain; SpaceLink Australia investment wound down 2022, no operating Australian subsidiary identified (EV-GERMANY-09, EV-GERMANY-10, EV-GERMANY-20).

key_companies.name: Fraunhofer FHR
key_companies.note: GESTRA surveillance radar developer, 2015 DLR commission (EV-GERMANY-08).

key_companies.name: Rocket Factory Augsburg (RFA)
key_companies.note: RFA ONE maiden campaign at SaxaVord; 2022 Whalers Way launch services agreement assessed dormant (EV-GERMANY-15, EV-GERMANY-16).

key_companies.name: HyImpulse

key_companies.name: Isar Aerospace

germany.caveats: SARah operational status post-launch and GESTRA post-2023 handover status are not evidenced. German industrial workforce numbers are absent. The NewSpace launch-firm records are partly ASSESSMENT-grade (RFA) and the Australian-link findings are negative or dormant (OHB, RFA), logged in the germany.md validation backlog.

uae.summary: The UAE's evidenced industrial story is state-centred on the Mohammed bin Rashid Space Centre (MBRSC) rather than named private firms. MBZ-SAT — a 750 kg high-resolution Earth-observation satellite launched 14 January 2025 on a SpaceX Falcon 9 — was developed by Emirati engineers at MBRSC with approximately 90 per cent of mechanical structures sourced from UAE companies, delivering processed imagery within two hours of capture (EV-UAE-08, FACT); the supplying companies are not named in the register. The Emirates Mars Mission 'Hope' orbiter was developed by MBRSC with US university partners and launched on a Mitsubishi H-IIA in July 2020 (EV-UAE-07, corrected wording). MBRSC will provide the Crew and Science Airlock for the lunar Gateway, plus engineering support for the station's life, in exchange for an Emirati astronaut flight (EV-UAE-10). The register records no sovereign launch capability — both flagship spacecraft flew on foreign vehicles — and is silent on SDA, SATCOM operators, PNT, ground-segment sites and workforce numbers (uae.md paragraph 3 gap note). From 10 July 2026, BIS reclassification of the UAE to EAR Country Group A:5 gives licence-free eligibility for Commerce-controlled military items and certain commercial satellites and spacecraft (EV-UAE-14).

key_companies.name: Mohammed bin Rashid Space Centre (MBRSC)
key_companies.note: State space centre and de facto integrator: Hope orbiter, MBZ-SAT, Gateway Crew and Science Airlock (EV-UAE-07, EV-UAE-08, EV-UAE-10).

uae.caveats: No private UAE space company is named anywhere in the register — the ~90 per cent local-content claim for MBZ-SAT structures is uncredited to specific firms. National SATCOM operators, SDA industry and workforce numbers are register silences logged in the uae.md validation backlog.

pacific.summary: The register records no sovereign space system owned by the Pacific Islands Forum or any Pacific island member, and no Tech-industry capability held by PIF members; absence of record is not evidence of absence (pacific-pif.md paragraph 3). The recorded industrial story is connectivity infrastructure and foreign commercial LEO uptake: Starlink is leading, Amazon Leo enters in 2026, and the Chinese-backed GuoWang and Qianfan constellations are advancing (EV-PACIFIC-06). Terrestrial connectivity is fragile — single-cable dependency for Kiribati, Tuvalu, Vanuatu and Solomon Islands, with many PNG communities unconnected (EV-PACIFIC-06). The South Pacific Connect cable initiative (AU$80 million, announced late 2023) involves the US, Google and Vocus (EV-PACIFIC-07, Medium confidence). The only space-industrial activity on regional territory recorded is Australian-owned and Australian-run: the Cocos (Keeling) Islands ISRO TT&C ground station, commissioned by Australian company Nova Systems in July 2026 for India's Gaganyaan program — Australian territory, not PIF capability (EV-PACIFIC-18, EV-QUADINDI-07). There is no evidenced Pacific-owned space industry to summarise; the relevant industrial dynamics are foreign constellations competing for Pacific connectivity markets and allied cable investment.

key_companies.name: SpaceX (Starlink)
key_companies.note: Leading commercial LEO provider in the Pacific per the register's connectivity record (EV-PACIFIC-06).

key_companies.name: Vocus
key_companies.note: Partner with the US and Google in the AU$80 million South Pacific Connect cable initiative (EV-PACIFIC-07, Medium).

key_companies.name: Nova Systems
key_companies.note: Australian company that commissioned the Cocos (Keeling) Islands ISRO TT&C terminal, July 2026 (EV-PACIFIC-18, EV-QUADINDI-07).

pacific.caveats: No Pacific-owned space industry is recorded at all; every company in this snapshot is foreign to the PIF membership. GuoWang/Qianfan progress and Amazon Leo entry rest on a single Lowy-derived record. This is a structural finding about the partner, but coverage is also one record deep.

multilateral.summary: Multilateral groupings hold no industrial base of their own; what the register evidences is the industrial-access environment the groupings create. The AUKUS licence-free environment is the dominant record: the April 2024 EAR rule removed NS1/RS1/MT1 licence requirements for Australia and the UK, covering most 9x515 satellite items and 600-series military items — over US$7.5 billion per year of trade made licence-free (EV-AUKUSLFE-06); the ITAR paragraph 126.7 exemption operates within the three territories, with more than 700 Australian and UK Authorized Users enrolled by December 2025 (EV-AUKUSLFE-04); observed Australian uptake by February 2025 was 210-plus companies and A$25 million-plus in licence-free exports (EV-AUKUSLFE-13). Space-launch-vehicle technology remains excluded as MTCR-controlled (EV-AUKUSLFE-05). The single named industrial actor is Northrop Grumman, DARC developer under a US$341 million Site 1 contract (EV-USSFCSPO-14). The US-Australia TSA makes US commercial launch from Australia accessible under safeguards, with segregated-area rules that commentators assess may limit technology spillover to Australian industry (EV-AUKUSLFE-18, EV-AUKUSLFE-21, ASSESSMENT). The Quad's industrial expression is civil: the Australian-run, Quad-badged Cable Connectivity and Resilience Centre (EV-PACIFIC-07).

key_companies.name: Northrop Grumman
key_companies.note: DARC developer — the only company named against a grouping-badged program (US$341 million Site 1 contract) (EV-USSFCSPO-14).

multilateral.caveats: Category mismatch is the main caveat: groupings are trade-and-operations frameworks, not industrial actors, so this snapshot describes an access environment rather than a base. Uptake figures (210+ companies, A$25M+) are USSC think-tank estimates, and the spillover-limiting effect of TSA segregated areas is commentator assessment.

nz.summary: New Zealand ranks third globally for annual space launches (NZ-13, FACT), but the capability is not sovereign. Rocket Lab is US-domiciled — the New Zealand company became a subsidiary of the American parent around 2013; headquarters Long Beach, California; Nasdaq-listed 2021 (NZ-19, TO_VERIFY on detail) — operating Launch Complex 1 at Mahia from New Zealand geography under a treaty and segregated-area regime. MBIE's own permitting record shows a US Department of Defense rendezvous-and-proximity-operations mission (VICTUS HAZE Puma) permitted from New Zealand soil on 17 December 2025 (NZ-20, FACT); New Zealand has never declined a payload permit on national-interest grounds (NZ-21, FACT). The dossier assesses that Rocket Lab should be scored as a US capability operating from New Zealand geography, not a New Zealand contribution (new-zealand-round2-dossier.md paragraph 3a, ASSESSMENT). Civil SDA is outsourced to LeoLabs: the Kiwi Space Radar at Naseby (2019) and a multi-year MBIE agreement of August 2021 embed LeoLabs' platform in the NZ Space Agency's operations (NZ-17, NZ-18, FACT), and an NZDF squadron's sensor set includes a LeoLabs-operated South Island radar (NZ-13, FACT). Named NZ firms — Dawn Aerospace, Zenno Astronautics, Astrix Astronautics, Kea Aerospace, Xerra, Space Operations New Zealand — have no sourced defence contracts (TO_VERIFY).

key_companies.note: US-headquartered commercial SDA provider; Kiwi Space Radar (Naseby, 2019) and platform embedded in NZ Space Agency operations; also used by NZDF (NZ-13, NZ-17, NZ-18).

Rocket Lab corporate-history detail is secondary-sourced (TO_VERIFY); the LeoLabs contract value is withheld and unsourced; whether Kiwi Space Radar feeds the US SSN is repeated but unsourced either way; none of the six named NZ firms has a sourced defence contract.

canada.summary: The Canadian space-industrial base beyond MDA Space and Telesat is unresearched in this evidence base. A first-pass collection produced company-level claims that the collector subsequently retracted in full as fabricated — including an invented contract number — and the affected source keys (CA-18, CA-24) are retained as voids; no retracted claim may be reintroduced without primary sourcing (canada-round2-dossier.md paragraph 3a and collection integrity note). What is retained: MDA Space is the anchor — Q1 2026 revenue C$464.1 million, backlog C$3.7 billion, with the CHORUS SAR constellation targeted for late-2026 launch (CA-21, FACT) — holding the C$32 million Surveillance of Space 2 award (CA-11, FACT) and the C$688 million RCM replenishment contract of June 2026 (CA-15, FACT). Telesat Lightspeed: approximately 288 satellites, C$2.54 billion in funding agreements, 25 per cent of capacity allocated to military Ka-band (CA-22, FACT); its New South Wales landing station is built and operated by Vocus, with no ADF contract attached (CA-23, FACT). The A-OTHR arrangement (C$2.5 billion, BAE Systems Australia as industry partner) is over-the-horizon radar, not space (CA-25, FACT). Whether any Canadian firm holds an Australian defence contract is not established (CA-24, WITHDRAWN).

key_companies.name: MDA Space
key_companies.note: Canadian space prime: CHORUS, SoS 2 (C$32m), RCM replenishment (C$688m), enhanced SSA data services to DND (CA-11, CA-15, CA-21; VEH-CANADA-29).

key_companies.name: Telesat
key_companies.note: Lightspeed LEO constellation (~288 satellites, C$2.54bn funding, 25% military Ka-band); NSW landing station operated by Vocus, no ADF contract (CA-22, CA-23; VEH-CANADA-28).

key_companies.name: BAE Systems Australia
key_companies.note: Industry partner for the C$2.5 billion Canada-Australia A-OTHR acquisition — context only, not a space program (CA-25).

canada.caveats: Confidence is Low by direction of the round-2 dossier: the industrial base beyond MDA Space and Telesat is unresearched, not thinly sourced, after a fabrication retraction (CA-18 and CA-24 withdrawn as voids). Magellan Aerospace was tasked but not sourced (TO_VERIFY). Canadian industry presence in Australia is likewise unresearched. Evidence keys in the CA-xx namespace are the dossier's provisional source register (to be minted as topic canada-au on ingest).

france.summary: France fields the strongest evidenced space-industrial base in the European set, organised around two primes and a sovereign launch chain (france.md BLUF, ASSESSMENT). Airbus Defence and Space (Toulouse) built the three CSO optical reconnaissance satellites and co-built the CERES SIGINT triplet (EV-FRANCE-03, EV-FRANCE-05). Thales Alenia Space supplied the CSO optical instruments, co-built CERES and is co-prime for the ~€3.6 billion Syracuse IV milsatcom program (EV-FRANCE-03, EV-FRANCE-04, EV-FRANCE-05). ArianeGroup is prime for Ariane 6, operated by Arianespace from the Guiana Space Centre at Kourou; the launcher's first commercial flight (6 March 2025) orbited CSO-3 — a military payload on a national launcher from national territory (EV-FRANCE-07). The DGA/CDE ARES operation is developing the YODA geostationary patroller and TOUTATIS LEO demonstrators, with on-orbit and ground-based laser projects funded in the 2024-2030 LPM (EV-FRANCE-06). In Australia, the largest French industrial foothold is Thales Australia (~3,800 employees, 2023) — with no space or ground-station work in Australia evidenced (VEH-FRANCE-21, negative finding). The collection is one-round, and the industry lane's Australian angle rests on a single secondary source (france.md validation backlog).

key_companies.note: CSO platform prime (three satellites, 2018-2025); CERES co-builder (EV-FRANCE-03, EV-FRANCE-05).

key_companies.name: Thales Alenia Space
key_companies.note: CSO instruments; CERES co-builder; Syracuse IV co-prime (~€3.6bn) (EV-FRANCE-03, EV-FRANCE-04, EV-FRANCE-05).

france.caveats: One-round collection. The French industrial base is well evidenced at program level but the Australia-facing industry lane rests on one secondary source (Thales Australia negative finding); Thales Alenia Space / Airbus DS footprint in Australia is a validation-backlog item. The France baseline cites these vehicles as VEH-FR-17/VEH-FR-21; the canonical register IDs are VEH-FRANCE-17/VEH-FRANCE-21.

italy.summary: Italy pairs one of the most complete industrial stacks in the portfolio with a near-empty Australia channel (italy.md BLUF, ASSESSMENT). Leonardo is the defence prime — parent of Telespazio, co-parent of Thales Alenia Space — and carries a DFAT-recorded investment footprint in Australia (EV-ITALY-01; VEH-ITALY-13). Thales Alenia Space is prime for COSMO-SkyMed, the dual-use X-band SAR constellation whose second generation was still launching as of January 2026 (CSG-3; CSG-4 planned 2027) (EV-ITALY-07). Telespazio/e-GEOS (80/20 with ASI) holds exclusive worldwide commercial rights to COSMO-SkyMed data (EV-ITALY-07). Avio is national prime for the Vega C launcher, with ESA moving toward direct Avio commercialisation from August 2024 — launches occur from French Guiana, so this is capability without national territory (EV-ITALY-12). The IRIDE fast-deploying EO constellation (16 satellites on orbit after three 2025 launches; complete by end-2028) is built by Argotec, Officina Stellare, OHB Italia and Optec (EV-ITALY-11). SICRAL milsatcom capacity is shared among Italian defence, Telespazio and NATO (EV-ITALY-08). One-round collection; OPTSAT-3000 current status and the SICRAL next generation are unverified (italy.md paragraph 3).

key_companies.name: Leonardo
key_companies.note: Defence prime; parent of Telespazio, co-parent of Thales Alenia Space; DFAT-recorded investment footprint in Australia (EV-ITALY-01; VEH-ITALY-13).

key_companies.name: Thales Alenia Space
key_companies.note: COSMO-SkyMed prime — dual-use X-band SAR, second generation launching through January 2026 (EV-ITALY-07).

key_companies.name: Telespazio / e-GEOS
key_companies.note: e-GEOS (80/20 Telespazio-ASI) holds exclusive worldwide COSMO-SkyMed commercial data rights (EV-ITALY-07).

key_companies.name: Avio
key_companies.note: Vega C national prime; ESA moved toward direct Avio commercialisation, August 2024 (EV-ITALY-12).

key_companies.name: Argotec, Officina Stellare, OHB Italia, Optec
key_companies.note: IRIDE constellation builders (EV-ITALY-11).

italy.caveats: One-round collection. OPTSAT-3000 status (design life 7+ years, launched 2017) and SICRAL next-generation plans are unverified; national SDA sensor detail is not evidenced; Leonardo's Australian footprint is recorded by DFAT at investment level with no space content.

norway.summary: Norwegian space is a tight state-industrial triangle: the state owns the operator (Space Norway), most of the launch site (Andøya) and half the ground-segment company, with Kongsberg holding the other industrial corners — engagement with any node reaches the whole system (norway.md paragraph 2, ASSESSMENT). Space Norway operates ASBM, two ~2,000 kg Northrop Grumman-built HEO satellites (launched 12 August 2024) hosting a USSF EPS-R protected-communications payload, Inmarsat GX10A/10B Ka-band payloads and a Norwegian MoD X-band payload stated to be interoperable with the WGS constellation in which Australia holds assured access (EV-NORWAY-07, EV-NORWAY-08, EV-NORWAY-10). Kongsberg Satellite Services (KSAT, 50/50 Space Norway/Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace) runs a global network of 200-plus antennas anchored by SvalSat (78°N, the world's largest polar ground station) and TrollSat in Antarctica (EV-NORWAY-11). Andøya Spaceport hosted the first orbital launch attempt from continental Europe (Isar Aerospace's Spectrum, 30 March 2025) (EV-NORWAY-13). Kongsberg's large Australian presence is missile-industrial, not space: the Williamtown factory partnership (Commonwealth contribution up to $850 million) and the Mawson Lakes facility (EV-NORWAY-16, EV-NORWAY-17). NAMMO and Kongsberg's own smallsat activity were not evidenced this round (norway.md paragraph 3).

key_companies.name: Space Norway
key_companies.note: Wholly state-owned operator of the ASBM Arctic HEO SATCOM system with USSF, Inmarsat and Norwegian MoD hosted payloads (EV-NORWAY-07, EV-NORWAY-08).

key_companies.name: Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace
key_companies.note: Holds 10% of Andøya and 50% of KSAT; NSM/JSM missile lines; Kongsberg Defence Australia factory at Williamtown and facility at Mawson Lakes (EV-NORWAY-11, EV-NORWAY-13, EV-NORWAY-16, EV-NORWAY-17).

norway.caveats: One-round collection. NAMMO and Kongsberg smallsat activity were not evidenced; no Norwegian military space organisation record was collected; the entire evidenced Norway-Australia industrial relationship is missile-industrial with no space content — the space-industrial link to Australia is zero on the current record.

rok.summary: The ROK base spans launch, satellites and payloads, with one live industrial bridge to Australia. Hanwha Aerospace builds the Nuri launcher's engines, owns about 36 per cent of Satrec Initiative and invested ₩428.5 billion in OneWeb (EV-ROK-15, EV-ROK-16, EV-ROK-17); Hanwha Systems builds small SAR satellites, one orbited by the ADD solid-fuel launch vehicle's December 2023 sea-barge test (EV-ROK-16); and Hanwha already builds ADF vehicles in Geelong — the AS9 Huntsman/AS10 and AS21 Redback lines (EV-ROK-07, EV-ROK-08; VEH-ROK-11, VEH-ROK-12). KAI, quasi-public, assembles Nuri (EV-ROK-15); LIG Nex1 sits in the commercial base (EV-ROK-17); Satrec Initiative builds EO satellites and distributes KOMPSAT imagery through SI Imaging Services (EV-ROK-17). Foreign primes appear inside sovereign programs: ANASIS-II, the first dedicated military communications satellite, was Airbus-built as an F-35 offset (EV-ROK-14), and Thales Alenia Space was involved in the 425 Project SAR spacecraft — all five satellites launched on SpaceX Falcon 9 (EV-ROK-13). KASA runs a three-hub industrial cluster strategy: Sacheon (satellites), Daejeon (R&D), Goheung (launch) (EV-ROK-17). No ROK SDA/SSA industry is evidenced; the register is silent (republic-of-korea.md paragraph 3).

rok.caveats: One-round collection. No ROK SDA/SSA industry is evidenced. The Hanwha bridge to Australia is armoured vehicles, not space — no ROK space company has an evidenced Australian contract. KPS supply-chain detail and company financials beyond the Hanwha OneWeb figure were not collected.

singapore.summary: Singapore's base is an EDB-cultivated ecosystem with defence-lab lineage, evidenced around one prime. ST Engineering — via the 2011 joint venture of ST Electronics with NTU and DSO National Laboratories — built TeLEOS-1, Singapore's first commercial near-equatorial-orbit EO satellite (launched December 2015; 400 kg, 1 m optical resolution, 12-16 hour average equatorial revisit), and TeLEOS-2 (launched 22 April 2023) carrying a made-in-Singapore 1 m SAR payload (EV-SINGAPORE-10, EV-SINGAPORE-11); reported DSTA-ST Engineering joint development of TeLEOS-2 is TO_VERIFY (EV-SINGAPORE-11). DSO National Laboratories — 1,600-plus research scientists and engineers working across land, air, sea, space and cyberspace — launched TeLEOS-1, and DSTA is MINDEF's engineering statutory board (EV-SINGAPORE-12). OSTIn, under the Economic Development Board since 2013, grows the industry with a whole-of-government steering committee on which MINDEF sits but does not chair (EV-SINGAPORE-09); the reported ~2022 repositioning and S$150 million Space Technology Development Programme are plausible but unverified — EDB's web estate was bot-blocked (EV-SINGAPORE-17, TO_VERIFY). The ecosystem has attracted foreign operators such as SES since 2016 (EV-SINGAPORE-09). Industry headcounts and company counts were not verifiable this session, and there is no sovereign launch — both TeLEOS satellites flew on India's PSLV (EV-SINGAPORE-10, EV-SINGAPORE-11).

key_companies.note: Defence R&D institution (1,600+ research scientists and engineers); launched TeLEOS-1 (EV-SINGAPORE-12).

singapore.caveats: One-round collection with EDB's web estate bot-blocked: the S$150m STDP figure, industry headcounts and company counts are unverified. No Singaporean space regulator or licensing regime was evidenced. No Australia-Singapore space-industrial link of any kind is recorded.

domestic.summary: Capability exists across launch, SDA, smallsats and non-Earth imaging; what is missing is a stable, instrumented demand relationship with Defence (australian-industry-academia.md BLUF, ASSESSMENT). Gilmour Space Technologies holds Australia's first licensed commercial orbital spaceport (Bowen, 5 March 2024) and attempted the first sovereign orbital launch on 30 July 2025 — Eris crashed 14 seconds after lift-off; no sovereign orbital launch has yet succeeded (EV-DOMESTIC-11). Southern Launch operates the Whalers Way polar complex and the sub-orbital Koonibba Test Range (EV-DOMESTIC-13); ELA's Arnhem Space Centre, which hosted NASA's 2022 sounding-rocket campaign, ceased operations in December 2024 (EV-DOMESTIC-12). EOS Space Systems carries 40-plus years of laser/optical SDA and space-control heritage (EV-DOMESTIC-16); LeoLabs operates an Australian radar site (VEH-DOMESTIC-23); Saber Astronautics runs a Responsive Space Operations Centre in Australia (VEH-DOMESTIC-22); HEO provides non-Earth imaging with Defence and Intelligence as a customer segment but no named ADF contract (VEH-DOMESTIC-24). UNSW Canberra Space's RAAF-commissioned M-series is the clearest recurring Defence-to-academia procurement line (EV-DOMESTIC-15); Curtin's Binar program has flown four WA-built cubesats (EV-DOMESTIC-14). The flagship JP9102 SATCOM acquisition was cancelled on 4 November 2024 (EV-DOMESTIC-10). Fleet Space, Myriota, Advanced Navigation, Q-CTRL, Inovor, Optus and Skykraft are named in public reporting but were not fetched — TO_VERIFY.

domestic.caveats: One-round baseline with defence.gov.au bot-blocked, so the Defence side of every instrument is under-evidenced. SATCOM, PNT and ISR-EO at scale are not evidenced for any domestic firm; Fleet Space, Myriota, Advanced Navigation, Q-CTRL, Inovor, Optus and Skykraft were not fetched and nothing is asserted about them. EOS Defence contracts and the LeoLabs radar identity are TO_VERIFY.
